svg.title: Animated Cyber Incident Archive
svg.desc: One hundred cybersecurity incidents shown one at a time in descending year order, each with attack vector, impact and significance.

g.text: Generative AI can help craft convincing phishing, impersonation and multilingual lures.
Users and organisations face increased risk of credential theft and fraudulent approvals.
Raises the importance of out-of-band verification and phishing-resistant authentication.
Attackers target refresh tokens, consent grants and misconfigured app permissions.
Cloud email, storage and SaaS data may be accessed without repeated password prompts.
Highlights the need for token monitoring, conditional access and OAuth governance.
Compromised dependencies, build pipelines or maintainer accounts can distribute malicious updates.
Downstream users may inherit compromise through trusted software.
Makes provenance, dependency inventory and signed, reproducible builds critical.
Operators steal data before encrypting systems and threaten public disclosure.
Victims face recovery costs, operational outages, regulatory exposure and extortion pressure.
Backups alone are insufficient; detection, data controls and response planning are essential.
Threat actors exploit exposed or unpatched VPN, firewall and edge-device vulnerabilities.
Initial access can enable credential theft, lateral movement and persistent footholds.
Internet-facing infrastructure requires rapid patching, hardening and threat hunting.
Attackers used a compromised credential to access a student information system environment.
Student, parent and educator information at many school districts was affected.
Highlighted identity security and vendor concentration in education technology.
A cyberattack involving social engineering and compromised third-party access disrupted operations.
Online orders, payments and some store processes were affected.
Showed how identity-led intrusions can create prolonged retail and supply-chain disruption.
Attackers compromised systems and the retailer took systems offline as a containment measure.
Customer data was accessed and retail operations experienced disruption.
Demonstrated the trade-off between containment and business continuity.
A cyber incident led to shutdowns of key IT and manufacturing systems.
Vehicle production and supplier operations were significantly disrupted.
Illustrated the economic impact of cyber incidents on interconnected manufacturing supply chains.
Attackers abused stolen tokens, OAuth grants and over-permissioned integrations.
Cloud mailboxes, files and connected business applications were at risk.
Shows why OAuth consent, token lifetime and app permissions need continuous governance.
Threat actors used stolen credentials, MFA fatigue and remote-management tools for access.
Victims faced data theft, encryption and operational disruption.
Reflects the shift toward identity compromise as a common ransomware entry path.
ALPHV/BlackCat affiliates reportedly used compromised credentials on a remote access portal lacking
Prescription processing and healthcare payment operations were widely disrupted.
Showed how a single healthcare technology provider can create systemic sector disruption.
A password-spray attack against a legacy non-production account enabled access to corporate email.
Some senior leadership and cybersecurity team email communications were accessed.
Demonstrated the risk of legacy identities, weak passwords and inadequate MFA coverage.
A malicious maintainer contribution introduced a backdoor into XZ Utils release builds.
Potential SSH compromise affected certain Linux distributions; discovery preceded broad
A high-impact open-source supply-chain near miss exposing maintainer-trust risks.
Attackers used stolen credentials, often without MFA, to access customer Snowflake environments.
Multiple organisations reported theft of customer and employee data.
Highlighted cloud identity hygiene, MFA enforcement and third-party data-platform monitoring.
Attackers accessed data hosted in a third-party cloud environment associated with Snowflake.
Customer information, including contact and payment-related data, was reportedly offered for sale.
Showed how compromised cloud credentials can expose large customer datasets.
Qilin ransomware disrupted a pathology services provider supporting NHS organisations.
Blood testing and clinical services in London were significantly disrupted.
Demonstrated the patient-care consequences of attacks on healthcare suppliers.
A ransomware attack disrupted the automotive retail software provider's systems.
Thousands of car dealerships experienced outages in sales and service operations.
Showed concentration risk when many businesses depend on one SaaS provider.
A data broker database was reportedly exposed and circulated by threat actors.
Large volumes of personal information, including Social Security numbers, were reportedly involved.
Highlighted data-broker security, retention and identity-theft risks.
A ransomware incident affected the health system's IT environment.
Clinical workflows, patient care and hospital operations were disrupted.
Reinforced the need for resilient clinical operations and tested recovery plans.
Attackers exploited a compromised BeyondTrust support key to access a remote support service.
Some Treasury workstations and unclassified documents were accessed.
Highlighted the risk of trusted third-party remote-support tools and secrets management.
Cl0p exploited a SQL injection zero-day in internet-facing MOVEit Transfer servers.
Many organisations and millions of individuals had personal data exposed.
A major mass-exploitation campaign against a widely used file-transfer product.
Social engineering of the IT help desk helped attackers compromise identity systems.
Hotel, casino and booking operations were disrupted for days.
Showed how identity-provider compromise can create large-scale business disruption.
Attackers reportedly used social engineering to compromise an outsourced IT support provider.
Customer loyalty data was stolen and the company reported a ransom payment.
Highlighted third-party access and social-engineering risks in hospitality.
A compromised software build chain led to a trojanised 3CX desktop application.
Downstream customers installing the application were exposed to follow-on malware.
A rare multi-stage supply-chain compromise affecting trusted enterprise software.
A compromised signing key was used to forge authentication tokens and access mailboxes.
Selected government and enterprise email accounts were accessed.
Highlighted cloud identity key management and token-validation security.
An exposed API allowed unauthorised access to customer account information.
Approximately 37 million customer accounts were affected.
Reinforced API authentication, authorisation and rate-limiting requirements.
Conti ransomware operators compromised government systems and demanded payment.
Multiple government services were disrupted and a national emergency was declared.
Demonstrated the potential for ransomware to affect public administration at national scale.
Attackers accessed a third-party support provider's environment and support data.
Some Okta customer support files and session-related information were accessed.
Highlighted identity-provider supply-chain exposure and support-access controls.
An attacker used social engineering and MFA fatigue to obtain employee access.
Internal systems and security tools were accessed; operations and data were at risk.
Showed the importance of phishing-resistant MFA and help-desk verification.
An attacker compromised a developer environment and later accessed encrypted customer vault backups.
Customer vault data and account metadata were stolen; master-password strength became critical.
Demonstrated how developer access can lead to high-value production and backup exposure.
Attackers compromised validator keys and forged withdrawal approvals.
Approximately $625 million in cryptocurrency was stolen.
Showed the systemic risk of concentrated signing authority and weak key governance.
A smart-contract verification flaw enabled forged messages and unauthorised token minting.
About $320 million in cryptocurrency was stolen.
Highlighted the importance of smart-contract audits and cross-chain validation.
Social engineering, credential theft and help-desk manipulation enabled access to corporate
Several technology companies reported source-code or internal-data exposure.
Showed that identity compromise and human-focused attacks can bypass technical controls.
Conti's internal communications and operational data were leaked amid the ransomware campaign.
Researchers gained insight into the group's infrastructure, tactics and affiliates.
Provided valuable intelligence on ransomware organisation and tradecraft.
Attackers exploited ProxyLogon vulnerabilities in on-premises Exchange servers.
Thousands of organisations faced web shells, mailbox access and follow-on ransomware.
Showed the danger of exposed email infrastructure and delayed emergency patching.
DarkSide ransomware operators accessed IT systems using a compromised VPN account.
The company halted pipeline operations, causing fuel-supply disruption in the eastern US.
Demonstrated how IT ransomware can create real-world critical-infrastructure consequences.
REvil exploited vulnerabilities in the VSA remote-management platform to distribute ransomware.
Managed service providers and many downstream customers were affected.
Showed how trusted remote-management tools can multiply supply-chain impact.
Attackers exploited zero-day vulnerabilities in the legacy file-transfer appliance.
Multiple organisations suffered data theft and extortion.
Highlighted the risk of unsupported edge appliances and sensitive file-transfer systems.
A chain of Exchange Server vulnerabilities enabled unauthenticated remote code execution.
Internet-facing Exchange servers were compromised at scale.
Reinforced the need for asset inventory, emergency patching and post-exploit hunting.
REvil ransomware disrupted corporate IT systems at the global meat producer.
Production was temporarily halted at facilities in several countries.
Showed the potential supply-chain and food-production impact of ransomware.
An attacker accessed systems and exfiltrated customer data.
Data relating to tens of millions of current, former and prospective customers was exposed.
Emphasised identity-data protection and continuous monitoring of external access.
A JNDI lookup flaw in Apache Log4j enabled remote code execution in vulnerable applications.
A broad range of enterprise products and internet services required urgent remediation.
One of the most pervasive software vulnerabilities; exposed dependency-inventory gaps.
Attackers trojanised a software build/update process to distribute a signed backdoor.
Government agencies and enterprises were compromised through trusted updates.
A defining software supply-chain intrusion with long-dwell espionage consequences.
Social engineering of employees gave attackers access to internal administration tools.
High-profile accounts were hijacked to promote a cryptocurrency scam.
Demonstrated that privileged support workflows are vulnerable to human manipulation.
A ransomware incident disrupted corporate systems and connected services.
Customer-facing services, aviation products and manufacturing operations were affected.
Showed how ransomware can disrupt both IT and operational service delivery.
Attackers accessed hosted systems and exfiltrated customer data before ransomware deployment.
Universities, charities and their constituents faced data exposure.
Highlighted concentration risk in SaaS providers and third-party incident management.
A misconfigured web application firewall and SSRF technique enabled cloud metadata access.
Approximately 100 million people in the US and Canada were affected.
Showed how cloud IAM permissions and metadata services can amplify configuration flaws.
Attackers exploited vulnerabilities in Citrix ADC and Gateway appliances.
Multiple organisations faced unauthorised access and potential data theft.
Emphasised rapid patching of internet-facing VPN and gateway appliances.
A large aggregation of previously stolen credentials was circulated online.
Hundreds of millions of email/password combinations were exposed or recirculated.
Illustrated the continuing risk of password reuse and credential stuffing.
A cybercriminal marketplace was breached, exposing stolen payment-card inventory.
Millions of compromised card records were reportedly exposed to investigators.
Showed the scale of underground payment-card trading and value of threat intelligence.
Attackers maintained unauthorised access to the Starwood reservation database.
Personal information for hundreds of millions of guests was exposed.
Highlighted merger-related security risks and the importance of legacy-system diligence.
Attackers compromised a front-end workstation and moved into patient-data systems.
Personal data of approximately 1.5 million patients, including the Prime Minister, was accessed.
Showed the need for segmentation and strong monitoring in healthcare networks.
A publicly accessible database was left exposed without adequate access protection.
Hundreds of millions of consumer and business contact records were potentially exposed.
A prominent example of cloud/database exposure caused by misconfiguration.
Injected JavaScript captured payment details entered on the airline's website.
Payment information for roughly 380,000 transactions was compromised.
Highlighted client-side supply-chain risks and the need to monitor web scripts.
Used the EternalBlue SMBv1 exploit to spread rapidly between vulnerable Windows systems.
Hundreds of thousands of systems were affected, disrupting hospitals and businesses.
Showed the global impact of unpatched vulnerabilities and wormable ransomware.
A compromised software update delivered destructive malware that spread through networks.
Global companies suffered major operational outages and billions in losses.
A major supply-chain attack whose destructive impact exceeded conventional ransomware.
Attackers exploited an unpatched Apache Struts vulnerability in a web application.
Sensitive personal data of approximately 147 million people was exposed.
Illustrated the consequences of delayed vulnerability remediation in public-facing systems.
A Cloudflare parser bug caused memory contents to leak into web responses.
Potentially exposed cookies, passwords and other data across affected websites.
Demonstrated that software bugs in shared infrastructure can expose many customers.
Attackers compromised bank systems and abused SWIFT payment workflows.
Fraudulent transfer requests attempted to steal nearly $1 billion; about $81 million was lost.
Exposed the need for transaction validation and secure financial messaging controls.
Default or weak credentials were used to compromise IoT devices into a DDoS botnet.
Dyn's DNS services were disrupted, affecting many major websites.
Showed how insecure consumer IoT devices can threaten internet-scale availability.
Spear-phishing and credential theft provided access to political organisation networks.
Emails and internal documents were stolen and publicly released.
Highlighted risks to election integrity, sensitive communications and organisational trust.
The company disclosed a previously unknown 2014 intrusion involving account data theft.
Approximately 500 million accounts were initially reported affected.
Demonstrated how delayed discovery and disclosure can compound breach impact.
Attackers accessed private GitHub credentials and used them to reach cloud-hosted data.
Data relating to 57 million riders and drivers was exposed.
Showed why secrets must not be committed to source repositories and breaches must be disclosed.
Attackers used stolen credentials and targeted database access to obtain member records.
Nearly 79 million current and former members were affected.
Highlighted the sensitivity of identity and health-insurance data.
Intruders used compromised credentials and lateral movement to access personnel databases.
Sensitive records of more than 20 million people were exposed.
Demonstrated the long-term intelligence value of government personnel data.
Attackers breached the service and exfiltrated user and internal company data.
Account details and private information were publicly exposed.
Showed the personal safety and reputational consequences of data breaches.
Spear-phishing and BlackEnergy malware enabled operators to access utility control systems.
A landmark case of cyber operations disrupting critical infrastructure.
Attackers used compromised employee credentials to access a corporate database.
Personal information for roughly 145 million users was exposed; password reset was required.
Showed the importance of employee account security and breach response.
A destructive intrusion used malware and stolen data; attribution was disputed.
Corporate data, unreleased films and employee information were leaked; systems disrupted.
Combined destructive operations, extortion and large-scale data disclosure.
Compromised vendor credentials and POS malware enabled payment-card data theft.
Payment-card details for tens of millions of customers were exposed.
Reinforced POS hardening, third-party access control and network segmentation.
Attackers exploited the Heartbleed OpenSSL vulnerability to obtain user information.
Personal information of approximately 4.5 million patients was affected.
Showed how infrastructure vulnerabilities can expose regulated healthcare data.
Attackers used a compromised employee account and exploited an unpatched web server to move through
Contact information for approximately 76 million households and 7 million small businesses was
Showed that perimeter compromise and excessive access can expose large customer datasets.
Stolen third-party vendor credentials enabled access; malware collected payment data at POS
Payment-card data and customer contact information for millions were exposed.
Showed how vendor access can become a path into critical business systems.
Attackers accessed corporate systems and exfiltrated account credentials and source code.
Tens of millions of customer accounts were affected; source code was stolen.
Highlighted password storage, credential reuse and intellectual-property exposure risks.
Attackers used forged cookies and compromised account data to access user accounts.
All three billion Yahoo accounts were ultimately reported affected.
One of the largest account-data breaches; exposed risks from weak credential protection.
Highly sophisticated malware used targeted delivery and Windows network techniques for espionage.
Selected systems in the Middle East were surveilled and sensitive data collected.
Illustrated cyber-espionage capabilities beyond conventional destructive malware.
Malware used stolen credentials and a destructive wiping component to attack Windows systems.
Thousands of workstations at Saudi Aramco were rendered unusable.
Demonstrated the operational impact of destructive malware against enterprise endpoints.
A targeted phishing email with a malicious attachment compromised an employee system.
Information related to SecurID authentication products was stolen.
Demonstrated how an initial foothold can threaten downstream customers and trust.
Attackers compromised network infrastructure; the exact initial vector was not publicly established.
Personal data for approximately 77 million accounts was exposed; service was suspended.
Highlighted breach disclosure, service resilience and protection of user identity data.
An attacker issued fraudulent TLS certificates after compromising the certificate authority.
Fake certificates were used to intercept some users' encrypted sessions.
Undermined trust in the certificate ecosystem and accelerated CA security scrutiny.
Used multiple Windows zero-days and stolen certificates to reach industrial control environments.
Damaged centrifuges at an Iranian nuclear facility while masking operational changes.
Showed that malware can cause physical effects in industrial environments.
Spear-phishing emails installed malware that enabled remote surveillance.
Government, diplomatic and other organisations had systems monitored.
Exposed the espionage risk of targeted phishing and long-term access.
Targeted spear-phishing and browser exploitation enabled access to corporate networks.
Google and other organisations reported intellectual-property and account-access risks.
Raised awareness of advanced persistent threats and software supply-chain trust.
Removable media introduced malware that spread across military networks.
Sensitive networks faced a major cleanup and remediation effort.
Led to stricter removable-media controls and improved endpoint safeguards.
Exploited Windows vulnerabilities and weak passwords; spread through networks and removable media.
Millions of systems were infected worldwide.
Showed the persistence of unpatched systems and the challenge of global remediation.
Malware on the payment network captured card data during transaction processing.
Tens of millions of payment-card records were exposed.
Emphasised segmentation, continuous monitoring and secure payment processing.
Large-scale traffic floods targeted government, banking and media websites.
Online services across the country were disrupted for weeks in some cases.
Demonstrated national-level dependence on resilient digital infrastructure.
Intruders exploited weak wireless security and accessed payment systems.
Tens of millions of payment-card and personal records were affected.
Became a major case study in network security and payment-card protection.
Attackers accessed payment-processing systems and exposed unencrypted transaction data.
Millions of payment-card records were reportedly exposed.
Highlighted the need for payment-data minimisation, encryption and access controls.
Spread through email attachments and peer-to-peer sharing; installed backdoor functionality.
Became one of the fastest-spreading email worms and enabled DDoS activity.
Showed how mass-mailing malware can combine infection, remote access and disruption.
Exploited a SQL Server resolution-service buffer overflow over UDP 1434.
Spread globally within minutes, congesting networks and disrupting services.
A landmark example of the speed of memory-corruption worm propagation.
Exploited the Windows RPC DCOM vulnerability and scanned for vulnerable hosts.
Triggered system instability and outages across home and enterprise networks.
Reinforced the importance of emergency patching and network segmentation.
Exploited an IIS buffer-overflow vulnerability and spread by scanning networks.
Hundreds of thousands of servers were infected; government and business sites were disrupted.
Accelerated patching and perimeter exposure management for internet-facing servers.
Combined email, web-server exploitation, network shares and infected websites.
Rapidly compromised enterprise networks and consumed bandwidth and administrator time.
Illustrated how one worm can use several propagation paths simultaneously.
A VBScript attachment used social engineering and Outlook contacts to propagate.
Millions of Windows systems were affected; organisations incurred major recovery costs.
Showed the destructive reach of email-borne malware and unsafe scripting defaults.
Compromised systems were coordinated to flood major websites with traffic.
CNN, Yahoo, eBay and other high-profile services suffered outages.
Put distributed denial-of-service attacks and botnet control in the public spotlight.
A malicious Word document macro spread through Microsoft Outlook address books.
Mail systems at many organisations were overloaded and business operations disrupted.
Demonstrated how trusted email attachments can amplify malware at scale.
Attackers used compromised credentials and remote access to initiate unauthorised transfers.
More than $10 million was targeted; most funds were recovered.
Highlighted the financial risk of weak authentication and cross-border cybercrime.
Exploited Unix sendmail, fingerd and weak passwords to self-propagate.
Infected roughly 6,000 computers, disrupting a significant part of the early Internet.
One of the first major Internet worms; exposed the need for coordinated incident response.
